title: How to organise the bench and transition surface | Mudroom
description:
Somewhere to sit while you deal with your footwear, and a brief stop for things genuinely on their way out of the house.

This is the Bench and Transition Surface in the Mudroom. About 15-30 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
A bare seat wide enough for two people to lace boots at once, no more than three objects on the surface, and one labelled basket at the end holding only what is leaving tomorrow.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Clear the bench down to bare wood in one go.
Straighten: Protect the seat itself as empty space and give the strays one outbound basket: the library books, the parcel
Shine: Wipe the seat and the front edge where boot heels scuff it, then pull the bench away from the wall and sweep o
Safety: Nothing heavy stores on a shelf above the seat, because a bike helmet or a paint tin landing on someone bent o
Standardize: Three objects maximum on the surface, and the outbound basket empties on the next trip out of the door.
Sustain: When you sit down to change your shoes, take one thing off the bench into the house with you as you stand up.

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
The seat is always clear, and the surface never carries more than three things.

Full written steps for this zone, free:
https://6s-success.com/zones/mudroom-the-bench-and-transition-surface.html

6S Success turns Lean's six-S method into something you can actually do in a house: Sort, Straighten, Shine, Safety, Standardize, Sustain. One small zone at a time, finished in one session, and it stays finished.
